creator: bengusberg
title: Google Labs 'Little Language Lessons' free AI language-learning experiments (Tiny Lesson, Slang Hang, Word Cam)

tools.name: Tiny Lesson
tools.detail: Vocab and grammar 'like a traditional tutor'

tools.name: Slang Hang
tools.detail: Teaches slang/regional expressions 'so you sound like a native'

tools.name: Word Cam
tools.detail: Snap a photo, learn to talk about what is in it

claims: Google launched a free AI platform teaching 20+ languages (Japanese, Chinese, French, Spanish named)
Three free learning paths: Tiny Lesson, Slang Hang, Word Cam
Uses AI throughout to personalize to goals
Creator: 'Stanford founder of an AI startup, raised $4 million'
how_to_steps: Go to labs.google/lll/en and sign up for free
Pick one of the three experiments (Tiny Lesson / Slang Hang / Word Cam) and 'Try it'
on_screen_only: Browser URL bar: labs.google/lll/en with 'Google Labs EXPERIMENT' header

Cards: 'Tiny Lesson — Find relevant vocabulary, phrases, and grammar tips for any situation', 'Slang Hang — Learn expressions, idioms, and regional slang from a generated conversation between natives', 'Word Cam — Snap a photo to learn how to speak about your surroundings', each with 'Try it' button
cta: Try it and let me know what you learn; follow for AI, founder life, leadership

relevance.why: Consumer language-learning demo, not a dev or business tool. Only tangentially a reference for how Google packages small Gemini-powered apps.

implement_score.why: Nothing to adopt. If ever building a learning-app product, Word Cam (photo-to-lesson) is a cheap pattern to copy with a vision model.

verify: Is Little Language Lessons still live at labs.google/lll and free?
Is 20+ languages accurate? Is it 'Google Labs experiment' (may be shut down) rather than a product?
Does the 'killed Duolingo' framing have any substance?
